title: Constructive IVT via Bisection Algorithm
description: Formalizes the constructive content of the Intermediate Value Theorem via the bisection algorithm. Proves the bisection interval halves in width each step ((b-a)/2^n), maintains the sign invariant f(left) ≤ 0 ≤ f(right), stays within [a,b], and — the main theorem — produces points x ∈ [a,b] with |f(x)| < ε for any ε > 0. Also proves uniqueness of the zero for strictly monotone f. 13 theorems, 3 definitions, 0 axioms.

bisect_width: after n steps, interval width = (b-a)/2^n (exact formula)

overview.historicalContext: The classical IVT is non-constructive: it asserts existence without giving a procedure. The constructive content — the bisection algorithm — was known for centuries but formalizing its precision guarantees requires careful handling of uniform continuity. This file formalizes the algorithm and proves it finds ε-approximate roots for any ε > 0.
overview.problemStatement: Give a formal bisection algorithm for continuous f: [a,b] → ℝ with f(a) ≤ 0 ≤ f(b). Prove the interval width decreases as (b-a)/2^n and that for any ε > 0 the algorithm finds x ∈ [a,b] with |f(x)| < ε.
overview.text: The bisection step tests the midpoint: if f(mid) ≤ 0, keep [mid, right]; otherwise keep [left, mid]. After n steps the width is exactly (b-a)/2^n. The sign invariant f(left) ≤ 0 ≤ f(right) is maintained throughout. For the approximate IVT: use uniform continuity on [a,b] (compact) to find δ such that |f(x)-f(y)| < ε when |x-y| < δ; choose n so (b-a)/2^n < δ; the midpoint x satisfies dist(x, left) < δ and dist(x, right) < δ, so |f(x) - f(left)| < ε and |f(x) - f(right)| < ε; since f(left) ≤ 0 and f(right) ≥ 0 this forces |f(x)| < ε.
overview.proofStrategy: bisect_width by induction using bisectStep_width at each step. bisect_sign by induction using bisectStep_sign. approx_ivt: extract δ from uniform continuity, choose n via exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one, then apply both sign inequalities and uniform continuity at the midpoint.
keyInsights: Width halving: bisectStep_width is proved by pure algebra (no induction needed)
Sign preservation: bisectStep always keeps f(left) ≤ 0 ≤ f(right)
Key bridge: uniform continuity converts δ-closeness to ε-closeness of f values
constructive_ivt_summary packages all three guarantees in one theorem
prerequisites: Uniform continuity on compact sets: Metric.uniformContinuousOn_iff

conclusion.summary: Constructive IVT via bisection: width = (b-a)/2^n, sign invariant preserved, ε-approximate roots found for any ε > 0. 13 theorems, 0 axioms, 243 lines.
conclusion.implications: This formalization shows that the classical IVT has explicit computational content: bisection is a provably correct root-finding algorithm. The approach connects constructive and classical mathematics within Lean/Mathlib.
openQuestions: Formalize the full classical IVT from the approximate version (take limit of bisection midpoints)
Prove convergence rate: bisection achieves linear convergence in the number of bits
